svg.text: Borda counts pairwise wins. DPO finds the Borda winner
Pairwise RLHF is social choice in disguise.
Borda(y) = number of pairwise matchups y wins across all voters
Equivalently: expected count of alternatives ranked below y by a random voter.
Theorem: the DPO-optimal policy upweights each response proportionally to its
Borda score against alternatives drawn from the reference policy.
DPO aggregates pairwise preferences by finding the response that wins the most head-to-heads.
Caveat: needs uniform pair sampling from pi_ref and a correct BT model. Pipelines rarely satisfy either.
Source: textbook ch 5.3 theorem, original plate. Shell 4: the connection.
